hypothesis: The e<=0.9 ceiling on linear accel_step decodability is at least partly a capacity limit. Setup: N=64, 4 layers, d_model=128 (twice the width of exp-20261016-014337-2921), m2 in [0.1, 1], e in [0, 0.9], data_seed 0, best-of-5 controls, seeds 70-72, 3000 steps. Prediction: final raw accel_step R2 at the best-margin layer is at least 0.08 above the same seeds' d_model=64 values (0.457/0.421/0.447 for seeds 70/71/72), while accel_step still beats its control. All values come from probes_final, unrounded. The layer-4 value is reported separately if the best layer differs. Because random controls rise with d_model, the comparison uses trained R2, and headroom-normalised margin is reported for description only. Growth from step 1000 to step 3000 is reported as same-layer control plus margin.
expected_if_true: In all 3 seeds, raw accel_step R2 is >= 0.537 / 0.501 / 0.527 (seeds 70/71/72), and the accel_step margin is >= required_margin.
expected_if_false: In at least 2 of 3 seeds, raw accel_step R2 is <= d_model=64 + 0.04 (<= 0.497 / 0.461 / 0.487). The e<=0.9 ceiling then does not move with width at fixed depth, which points to a limit of linear readout or of the representation rather than to capacity. Mixed outcomes are inconclusive.
